**Heating complete.**

The room temperature has reached **24.1 °C** at the 160-minute observation, and the heater is now switched back on (confirmed at the 170-minute observation) to hold it there.

Summary of what happened:
- The heater was turned on early in the batch (~80 min), when the room was well below target.
- Readings climbed steadily: 21.3 °C → 22.5 °C → 23.7 °C (~1.2 °C per 10-minute interval while heating).
- Once the reading approached 24 °C, I switched the heater off at ~150 min to avoid overshoot; by 160 min the temperature had settled near the target with only a small residual rise.
- Because the switch has no automatic control, I re-enabled it at 170 min so the room doesn't drift back down as heat is lost to the environment.

Monitoring cadence going forward: check the thermometer every couple of turns, and toggle the heater off when the next reading lands at or just above 24 °C (the room's thermal lag means it keeps rising for about one interval after the heater cuts out).

To counteract the downward trend and bring the temperature back toward a comfortable range, I will turn the heater **on** now.
